title: A screen of the mod, described in data
description: What a window of the mod is made of, in the closed vocabulary of UI/Components — so that a Core on another engine draws the same screen from the same document with its own interpreter (UniverseLib here, Godot's Control tree there). A document says the SHAPE: what is where, what it is named, what it says, and what it asks for. It never says a rule: what a label shows or whether a button is offered is decided in code, from the facts, and written into the screen by its `bind` names. ⚠ The vocabulary is closed on purpose (`kind`): a kind added here is a widget every interpreter has to draw — added in this enum, in Engine/ScreenDocument.Kinds and in every builder, together. Kinds: card, stack, row, spacer, label, button, status (2026-09-12/15); section, field, dropdown, list and `help` on any piece (2026-09-15, for the upload setup screen); tabs, tab, callout, collapsible (2026-09-16, for the main screen); title, checkbox (2026-09-16, for the upload screen); toast, and chrome.titleBar / chrome.pinned (2026-09-16, for the corner notification); slider, sub-tabs (tabs.contentsIn), captioned fields (2026-09-16, for the options and tools screens); templates, choice, chip (2026-09-16, for the rows of every list); parts — a document of templates alone, shared by screens — minWidth on a stack or row, the Accent surface, SectionPadding, and a row that asks for an act when pressed as a whole (2026-09-17, for the status card and the community list).

name.description: Stable identity: the key the window's position and size are remembered under.

part.description: True for a PART: a document of templates alone, with no size, chrome, header, body or footer — a piece several screens hold (the status card, the community list), described once in screens/parts/ and instantiated by its component into the host a screen leaves for it.

backdrop.description: Darken the game behind the window.

cardWidth.description: The width the body's cards are laid out for; the window's width minus its margins when absent.

help.description: The resting sentence of a help bar pinned above the footer, where the explanation of whichever control is hovered is shown. Present, the screen has the bar; absent, it has none. What each control says there is the code's.

titleBar.description: The bar with the screen's name and its close button. Off for a corner notification.

pinned.description: Hangs from a screen corner chosen at run time (a setting) instead of being centred: never dragged or resized by hand.

header.description: The fixed part between the title bar and the body: what must stay put while the body scrolls — a title, the state somebody reads before choosing a row. Absent for a screen whose body carries its own title.

footer.description: The fixed row of verbs at the bottom.

templates.description: Pieces the document describes but does not place: the code instantiates one per element of a list (a conflict, a font, a backup) into the host it names, with that element's acts. Each template is one root piece with its own names, slots and acts, which may repeat from one template to the next. A title has no place in one.

text.description: Either the words themselves (interface text, translated by the mod's own policy) or a `bind`: a slot the code writes at show time, named by what goes there.

minHeight.description: A named height of the theme, or pixels at the reference resolution.

spacing.description: A named spacing of the theme, or pixels.

scope.description: Where the verb writes once applied — the two facts EditScope.SideAfter turns into the mark beside the label (Local, Published, Both). Said as facts so that no product invents the mark.

name.description: Unique in the document; how the code reaches the piece.

visible.description: Hidden at first when false: the code shows it when its moment comes (a code row before a code exists).

help.description: What the help bar says while this piece is hovered. Only on a screen whose chrome declares a help bar; a sentence, in the interface's register.

stretch.description: Takes the height left in its host — a tab's card, so the tab fills the window.

then.description: A section inside a card: no edge, its own padding.

rowHeight.description: The buttons' row height; the theme's when absent. Smaller for a row of sub-tabs.

contentsIn.description: The name of the piece the tabs' contents go into — a tab of another row, for sub-tabs — built earlier in the document. The body when absent.

then.description: A row of tabs whose buttons sit where the piece is placed — the header, so they stay put — and whose contents go into the body (or into `contentsIn`), one stack per tab, shown one at a time.

format.description: How the value is written beside the knob: Percent draws 0.4 as 40%; PercentOrDefault in steps of 5% with 'default' at zero, for a size multiplier.

act.description: Asked for as the knob moves.

then.description: A captioned slider the code reads (Value) and sets; its value at show time is the code's.

text.description: The word on the tab, and the name the code selects it by.

then.description: One tab of a `tabs` piece, and nothing else's child.
A tinted box that speaks up — an update available, a warning.

title.description: The line somebody clicks to open it.

then.description: A block folded under its title until somebody opens it.

placeholder.description: Shown while the field is empty.

caption.description: Words before the field, on its row; captionWidth is their width.

scroll.description: A Multiline field that keeps its height and scrolls inside it, instead of growing with what it holds.

richText.description: False keeps markup as characters — the file's exact text, being edited.

act.description: Asked for as the text changes; absent when the code only reads the field when it needs it.

then.description: A text field the code reads and writes by name. What is typed is the code's; the field holds nothing else.

options.description: Where the choices come from. Never a list written here: the languages are the catalogue's, the same list in every product; `code` means the code sets the choices and the initial one at show time (a list read from the game, a server, a setting).

first.description: A choice placed before the languages — 'auto (Detect)' — for a list whose first answer is not a language.

stretch.description: Takes the width of its row instead of its own.

popupHeight.description: How tall the open list may be.

act.description: The verb the screen asks its code for when the choice changes.

fill.description: Takes the spare height as well; false for a list of a settled height.

empty.description: The sentence shown while the list holds no row.

then.description: A scrolling list whose rows the code builds at show time — a form, never a rule: how many rows and what they say is the code's.

fillHeight.description: Takes the spare height as well.

minWidth.description: The least width it keeps — a stripe, a host that must hold a widget of a known width.

then.description: A vertical stack. Without children it is a HOST the code fills at show time (rows built from what the screen is shown for, or a component of its own).

pad.description: Room inside the row, on all four sides.

padX.description: Room on the two sides; padY on the top and bottom. Each overrides pad on its axis.

surface.description: The background the theme paints under it. Accent is the product's own colour — a stripe, a mark.

act.description: Asked for when the row is pressed anywhere its own controls do not take — a list row chosen by a click on its words. The row lights on hover and dips on press like a control.

then.description: A line the code writes with a tone (Say/Show/Clear) — collapsed while it has nothing to say.
A short-lived message the code shows with a tone and takes away after its time — a hotkey's feedback. Hidden until shown.
A line's quality tag as the square the website draws (H, V, A, S, M). The letter is data, written by the code (Retag); built blank.

options.description: The words, one per verb of equal standing; the code reads which was picked (Selected) and may set it.

initial.description: Which word starts picked; -1 for none.

act.description: Asked for when a word is picked.

then.description: Two or more words of which one is picked — Use Local / Use Server. Once picked it cannot be told back to none: a screen that needs that instantiates it again.

policy.description: Dynamic for a title the code rewrites (a mode announced in the title itself).

then.description: The screen's title with the three-position scope switch beside it — which copy this screen writes to. On every screen that shows translation lines, without exception; the panel base holds it for the window's resizes, which is why the builder asks the panel to make it.

text.description: Its words. Absent, a bare box whose words are elsewhere on its row — a title and a description beside it.

act.description: Asked for when the box is ticked or unticked; absent when the code only reads the box.

then.description: A box with its words. The code reads it (IsOn) or is told when it changes (act).

policy.description: How the mod's own translation treats it. A bound text is written at show time, so it is Dynamic — unless marked Excluded, for a slot that holds a count, a date or somebody's own words, written as they are.

minWidth.description: Room to align its words in — a label without one is stretched instead when aligned away from the left.

fill.description: As wide as its words, or the rest of the row.

autoHeight.description: A paragraph that wraps grows to what it draws.

richText.description: False shows markup as characters instead of rendering it — the file's exact text, for a line being edited.

italic.description: Said only to override the role's own choice (a Hint is italic unless told otherwise).

wrap.description: False keeps the text on one line, overflowing rather than folding — a name, a tag, a mark.

size.description: Field: as tall as the text field it sits beside.

act.description: The verb the screen asks its code for when pressed. Every act named must be handled — a check says so.
